target_claim: The proof asserts that for an integer a, cont(b n q f) = a * cont(n f), i.e. that pulling an integer scalar a out of the content multiplies the content by a itself. This is false when a (or b) is negative, since the content of an integer polynomial is the GCD of its coefficients and is nonnegative; the correct identity is cont(a g) = |a| cont(g). The proof never splits on the sign of a or b, and the same omission propagates to the final line cont(q f) = (a/b)(1/n) cont(n f) = q cont f.
source_quote:
By the definition of [[Definition:Content of Rational Polynomial|content]], and using that $a \in \Z$:
:$\cont {b n q f} = a \cont {n f}$
